findings.title: Access-token matcher does not check the expected grant
findings.body: The grant occupies prefix indices 4 through 5, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5), and it rejects equality rather than inequality. For example, both `onrtac:<uuid>` and `onrtna:<uuid>` pass when the expected grant is `ac`. Consequently, the updated authorization-code, refresh, device, and CIBA assertions do not detect missing or incorrect grant context. Validate the prefix length and compare substring(4, 6) against the expected shortcut, rejecting mismatches.

findings.title: Shortcut contract recommends a length the decoder cannot accept
findings.body: The new getShortcut() contract recommends a three-letter shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires an exactly six-character context prefix and allocates exactly two characters to the grant. A custom grant following this documentation can register successfully and issue tokens, yet those tokens cannot be decoded by the same provider. Document the mandatory two-character length and validate it when registering grant shortcuts so incompatible values cannot silently produce undecodable token IDs.

findings.title: Unknown-grant test passes on a NullPointerException
findings.body: The test fixture never calls factory.postInit(), leaving sessionFactory null. Decoding the unregistered `ac` shortcut therefore reaches getGrantTypeByShortcut() and throws a NullPointerException while attempting to refresh the registry, rather than the intended IllegalArgumentException for an unknown grant. Catching any RuntimeException makes the test pass despite not exercising the expected rejection behavior. Supply a session-factory mock with an empty provider stream and assert the specific IllegalArgumentException.
